title: Internal typed event bus
goal: A small typed in-process event bus, plus the catalogue of internal agent-runtime events, that decouples the runner, state machine, permissions, locks and the session layer without global state.
scope_in: Generic `EventBus<M>` where `M` maps event names to payload types: `on`, `once`, `off`, `emit`, `stream` (async iterator), `listenerCount`; synchronous in-order dispatch to listeners registered at emit time.

Re-entrancy rule: an `emit` made from inside a handler is queued and dispatched after the current dispatch finishes (FIFO), so handlers never observe nested delivery; max queue depth 10 000 then `BusOverflow` is reported to `onError` and the event dropped.

Error isolation: a throwing or rejecting handler never stops other handlers; errors go to the injected `onError(err, eventName)`; async handlers are not awaited by `emit` (use `stream` for backpressure-aware consumers).
`stream(names, { buffer = 1000, overflow = 'drop-oldest' })` returns an `AsyncIterable` with a bounded buffer and `return()` that unsubscribes.

`AgentEventMap`: the catalogue of internal events (names use `domain:verb`, deliberately different from wire kinds): `agent:started`, `agent:prompt`, `agent:message_delta`, `agent:message_done`, `agent:tool_requested`, `agent:tool_result`, `agent:approval_needed`, `agent:approval_resolved`, `agent:state_changed`, `agent:context`, `agent:compaction`, `agent:exited`, `worktree:created`, `worktree:removed`, `lock:changed`, `lock:conflict`, `subagent:spawned`, `subagent:finished`; each payload typed with `agent_id` (`agt_`) and ids from `@centcom/protocol`.
`createBus<M>(opts: { onError; maxListeners = 100 })` factory; no module-level singleton.
scope_out: Emitting these events: runner (C013), state machine (C014), permissions (C015), locks (C018), sub-agents (C024).
Converting internal events to wire frames: session layer lanes.
Cross-process delivery (IPC): runner daemon in C013.
build_against: Pure TypeScript library; no I/O. Tests use plain functions and fake timers.
interfaces: `interface EventBus<M extends Record<string, unknown>> { on<K extends keyof M>(k: K, h: (p: M[K]) => void | Promise<void>): Unsubscribe; once<K extends keyof M>(k: K, h: (p: M[K]) => void): Unsubscribe; emit<K extends keyof M>(k: K, p: M[K]): void; stream<K extends keyof M>(ks: readonly K[], o?: { buffer?: number; overflow?: 'drop-oldest' | 'drop-newest' }): AsyncIterable<{ k: K; p: M[K] }>; listenerCount(k?: keyof M): number }`
`createBus<M>(o: { onError: (e: unknown, k: string) => void; maxListeners?: number }): EventBus<M>`

Payload example: `'agent:state_changed': { agent_id: AgentId; state: StateName; since: string }`; `'agent:approval_needed': { agent_id: AgentId; approval_id: ApprovalId; risk: 'low'|'medium'|'high'; expires_at: string }`.
acceptance: Handlers run in registration order; a handler registered during dispatch of event X is not called for that same X emit.
Emitting `b` from inside the handler of `a` delivers `b` only after all handlers of `a` have returned (ordering asserted with a log array).
A handler that throws leaves later handlers running and calls `onError` exactly once with the event name; an async handler rejection does the same without unhandled-rejection warnings.
`stream` with buffer 3 and drop-oldest, fed 10 events with a stalled consumer, yields the last 3 events; memory stays bounded (no buffer above 3 entries).
Unsubscribe is idempotent; after `return()` on a stream `listenerCount` is 0; adding the 101st listener to one event calls `onError` with `MaxListeners` but still registers it.
Dispatch cost: 1,000,000 emits to 3 handlers complete in < 1 s on CI.
Type test (tsd/`expectTypeOf`): `emit('agent:exited', {})` fails to compile when the payload type requires `agent_id`.
tests: property test: random subscribe/emit sequences preserve per-listener FIFO.
guardrails: MUST NOT use module-level state or a default global bus; each runner owns its bus instance.
MUST keep every queue and buffer bounded (10 000 emit queue, 1000 stream buffer by default).

MUST NOT put message text, file contents, paths or branch names into events meant for the wire path; internal events may carry them for local UI but the wire-bound ones (`agent:state_changed`, `agent:approval_needed`) carry ids and enums only, and a lint comment in the catalogue marks which payload fields are wire-safe.
Handler errors MUST NOT be swallowed silently: always reach `onError`.
failure_modes: Queue overflow -> event dropped, `onError(BusOverflow)` once per 1000 drops, bus continues.
Listener leak -> `MaxListeners` warning via `onError`; no automatic removal.
Emit after all listeners removed -> no-op.
notes: Event names are internal and not part of any contract. If the catalogue grows beyond ~25 events consider splitting per area; keep names stable because C013/C014/C015/C018/C024 depend on them.
